subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this single product-wide localization contract—including Gateway error metadata, recipient locale ownership, localized command and skill metadata, and release completeness gates—or narrow it into smaller owner-approved RFCs?
rationale: The proposal spans multiple product and compatibility boundaries, and source inspection cannot determine permanent ownership, release policy, or public plugin-contract direction without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve the unified direction
options.body: Obtain explicit Gateway, channel, plugin/package, command-catalog, and release-owner approval, then accept the RFC with its compatibility guarantees intact.

options.title: Narrow the first RFC
options.body: Limit acceptance to the internal locale registry and message kernel, leaving recipient storage, plugin metadata, and release gates for separate owner-specific proposals.

options.title: Pause the proposal
options.body: Keep the draft open without acceptance until product localization receives sponsorship and implementation capacity.

recommendation.title: Approve the unified direction
recommendation.body: Obtain explicit Gateway, channel, plugin/package, command-catalog, and release-owner approval, then accept the RFC with its compatibility guarantees intact.

likelyOwner.reason: The inspected history shows repeated merger and integration responsibility for the existing localization foundation, and the RFC requires a cross-product decision rather than a single-surface implementation review.
